entries.text: Benedict and child sexual abuse in the Roman Catholic Church:

entries.raw: **[[Pope Benedict XVI]] concludes his visit to [[Malta]]. Reports suggest he is trying to avoid discussing the recent child sex abuse scandal, on his first trip since the scandal broke. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/8627878.stm (BBC)]
entries.text: Pope Benedict XVI concludes his visit to Malta. Reports suggest he is trying to avoid discussing the recent child sex abuse scandal, on his first trip since the scandal broke.

entries.raw: **However, he does meet with some of those who survived abuse and expresses "shame and sorrow" for their suffering. [https://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/19/world/europe/19pope.html (''The New York Times'')] [http://edition.cnn.com/2010/WORLD/europe/04/18/pope.malta/?hpt=T1 (CNN)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/vaticancityandholysee/7603808/Pope-meets-with-Malta-sex-abuse-victims.html (''The Daily Telegraph'')] [http://english.aljazeera.net/news/europe/2010/04/201041813179466391.html (Al Jazeera)]
entries.text: However, he does meet with some of those who survived abuse and expresses "shame and sorrow" for their suffering.

entries.raw: *[[List of countries by Independence Day|Independence Day]] in [[Zimbabwe]]:
entries.text: Independence Day in Zimbabwe:

entries.raw: **[[Zimbabwe]] marks 30 years of independence from British-backed minority white rule. [http://english.aljazeera.net/news/africa/2010/04/201041851759342391.html (Al Jazeera)]
entries.text: Zimbabwe marks 30 years of independence from British-backed minority white rule.

entries.raw: **Residents celebrate with all-night parties, though civil rights group [[Women of Zimbabwe Arise]] ([[WOZA]]) claim four of its members were denied bail after being accused of staging an illegal protest against power cuts and high electricity tariffs, an act they deny they did. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/africa/8627813.stm (BBC)] [http://www.zimtelegraph.com/?p=7006 (''Zimbabwe Telegraph'')]
entries.text: Residents celebrate with all-night parties, though civil rights group Women of Zimbabwe Arise (WOZA) claim four of its members were denied bail after being accused of staging an illegal protest against power cuts and high electricity tariffs, an act they deny they did.

entries.raw: **[[President of Zimbabwe]] [[Robert Mugabe]], in a speech at [[Harare]]'s stadium, promises to continue his land seizure policy and transfer of control of foreign firms to locals as part of a black empowerment drive. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/04/18/AR2010041801529.html (''The Washington Post'')]
entries.text: President of Zimbabwe Robert Mugabe, in a speech at Harare's stadium, promises to continue his land seizure policy and transfer of control of foreign firms to locals as part of a black empowerment drive.

entries.raw: **Mugabe also asks that politically and racially driven violence in the country cease to be, the first time he has ever done this. [http://news.smh.com.au/breaking-news-world/zimbabwe-marks-30-years-of-independence-20100418-smrq.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')] [http://english.aljazeera.net/news/africa/2010/04/2010418134932669805.html (Al Jazeera)]
entries.text: Mugabe also asks that politically and racially driven violence in the country cease to be, the first time he has ever done this.

entries.raw: *President of China [[Hu Jintao]] visits survivors in the earthquake zone as the death toll climbs to more than 1,700 people. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/8627946.stm (BBC)]
entries.text: President of China Hu Jintao visits survivors in the earthquake zone as the death toll climbs to more than 1,700 people.

entries.raw: *The semi-finals of the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) cricket tournament are moved from [[Bangalore]] to [[Mumbai]] following the discovery of further explosive devices after yesterday's bombing. [http://english.aljazeera.net/sport/2010/04/2010418115110981754.html (Al Jazeera)]
entries.text: The semi-finals of the Indian Premier League (IPL) cricket tournament are moved from Bangalore to Mumbai following the discovery of further explosive devices after yesterday's bombing.

entries.raw: *Seven people are killed and twenty others are injured in a suicide car bomb attack on a police station in [[Kohat]], one day after [[April 2010 Kohat bombings|twin bomb attacks]] kill more than 40 people and wound at least 60 others at a camp for the displaced in the city. All the dead are civilians.  [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/south_asia/8627880.stm (BBC)] [http://english.aljazeera.net/news/asia/2010/04/201041844327780903.html (Al Jazeera)] [http://edition.cnn.com/2010/WORLD/asiapcf/04/18/pakistan.blast/index.html (CNN)]
entries.text: Seven people are killed and twenty others are injured in a suicide car bomb attack on a police station in Kohat, one day after twin bomb attacks kill more than 40 people and wound at least 60 others at a camp for the displaced in the city. All the dead are civilians.
